data.name: Remy
data.gender_notes: Remy is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Ram, meaning 'exalted' or 'high'. Ram was an ancient name for God in Canaan and means 'God of heavens'. In the New Testament, Remy is also the name of a French saint, Remigius, who was a bishop in Reims, France, in the 5th century. He is the patron saint of Paris and of archers and is said to have healed many people through his prayers. Thus, Remy carries both Biblical and saintly significance in Christian tradition.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of heavenly connection and divine guidance.
data.etymology: Remy belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of heavens.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Remy total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.long_meaning: Remi is a French diminutive form of Remy, meaning 'oarsman, remigium' or 'renowned, famous, fame'. The name Remy has its roots in the French word 'remi', derived from the Latin 'remigium', meaning 'oarsman'. However, the name Remy is also associated with the Latin 'renominare', meaning 'to make famous'. In Christian tradition, the name Remy is not directly related to any biblical figure or saint. Nevertheless, it has been used in various Christian cultures as a given name, often symbolizing strength, courage, and fame.

data.cultural_impact: The name Remy has French origin and was made popular in the Middle Ages by St. Remigius, who converted Clovis I, the first Christian king of France, in the historic baptismal font of Reims. In today's society, the name still holds a rich cultural significance, particularly in France.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Remy holds a deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Hebrew word Ram, meaning 'God of heavens'. In Christianity, it is also associated with St. Remigius, a bishop in Reims, France, who is considered a powerful intercessor and healer. The name Remy thus embodies both a connection to the divine and a connection to the healing power of the church.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Remy, meaning 'oarsman' in Old French, symbolizes the Christian's rowing through life's waters, guided by their faith. It also spiritually represents the passionate commitment to navigate through life's challenges, just as a skilled oarsman navigates through rough waters.

historical_references.reference: Saint Remigius, also known as Remy or Remigius of Reims, was a Frankish bishop and a pioneer in Christian evangelization in Gaul. He was born around 437 AD in the Roman province of Belgica Secunda. After receiving an education in Rome, Remigius returned to Gaul and was appointed bishop of Reims in 450 AD by Pope Leo I. His efforts in evangelizing the Franks were successful, and he is most famous for having baptized Clovis I, the first Christian king of the Franks, in 496 AD.
historical_references.context: Early Christianization of the Frankish population in Gaul

historical_references.reference: Saint Remigius of Rouen, also known as Remigius or Remi, was a bishop and a renowned theologian of the Frankish kingdom. He was born around 437 AD in the Roman province of Belgica Secunda. After studying in Rome, Remigius became a bishop in Rouen around 450 AD. He is most famous for his role in the development of the Roman liturgy in Gaul, and for his theological writings, particularly his commentary on the Gospels.
historical_references.context: Development of the Roman liturgy and theological scholarship in Gaul
